The Process

How it works.

You install Archie, build an agent, and message it from anywhere. Here’s the whole picture, one step at a time.

The handover

What handing something over looks like.

You message your agent the way you’d text a friend (“what’s on my calendar?” “move my 3 o’clock,” “catch me up on today’s meetings”). It goes away and works, comes back if it needs you, and tells you when it’s done.

It holds the things you’d otherwise carry in your head. Tell it once: the follow-up on Friday, the detail to check before the call. It keeps hold of it, and messages you first when the time comes.

A morning briefing nobody asked for twice

This one runs a Daily Briefing routine and sends it over Telegram. Nobody typed a command. It was installed once, and it has arrived every morning since.

What it hands you

A file on your computer, not text to copy out.

Ask a chat app for a spreadsheet and you get a table in a message that you select, copy, paste and fix. Your agent writes the actual file and tells you where it put it. There is no download, because it was never anywhere else.

What it can write

  • Tables: a real Excel workbook (.xlsx) or a plain .csv that opens in Excel, Numbers or Sheets
  • Documents: a real Word document (.docx), or Markdown, plain text or a web page
  • Data and cards: .json, a calendar file (.ics), or a contact card (.vcf)
  • Not PDFs, images, audio or video. It writes those nine kinds and nothing else

Why that list is short on purpose

  • It is an allowlist, not a filter on dangerous types. Anything not on it cannot be written at all
  • Every kind on it is inert: opening one shows text or a table, and none of them is something your computer runs on a double click
  • Your agent chooses the filename. It never chooses the folder. Files land in one place you were told about, and a copy stays in your Archie folder
  • Which matters because the text asking for a file has often passed through something we did not write

Your agent tells you the path when it is done, so a file written while you were out is one you can find from your phone. How that is kept safe →

No terminal, no code

You do not need to be technical.

Archie is a desktop app: no code, no config files, no terminal. Want a person beside you? That’s what guided setup is for.

The moving parts

How it all connects.

Your agent runs on your own computer, built from a handful of parts you choose. Here is the whole thing, everywhere it reaches, and the one place it waits.

The whole list

What you actually need.

Less than you’d think. Three things, and you probably have one of them already. A chat app makes four, and that one can wait: you can talk to your agent inside Archie itself.

1

A computer that stays on and connected

One you don’t mind leaving powered on, awake and online, because your agent can only answer while Archie is running. Already have one? Use it: a laptop needs to stay plugged in and set never to sleep, and we’ll sort that with you. If you’d rather buy for it, a Mac mini is the easy answer. What to run it on settles the machine, the network and what to skip, for your situation.

It runs on both Mac and Windows.

2

An account with an AI company

Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT), Google (Gemini), Groq, xAI (Grok), DeepSeek or Mistral, pay-as-you-go. Groq is cheapest, and its free tier cannot run Archie. Google’s free tier does work, and is the one Google trains on; its paid tier says it does not. Archie’s free credits run on Claude. What each company does with your words, before you pick. You pay for what your agent does: $1 to $7 a month for a handful of tasks a day, up to around $200 for one wired into a whole working day. Worked out for 3 levels of use. Billed straight to you, capped by you, never seen by us. The plan with the AI included has no second bill: $25 a month of it, inside the price.

Archie itself is $30 a month or $299 a year when it ships, a separate cost from guided setup. Every cost, in full.

3

An Otian account, and a plan

Archie asks you to sign in when it opens, and a browser window handles it. A plan is $30 a month or $299 a year, and you can change or stop it whenever you like. On our side it holds your email address and your plan. Never a conversation.

The same cost named above, not a second charge. Every cost, in full.

+

Optional: a chat app, to be reached anywhere

Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix or, on a Mac, iMessage. Not something to sort out before you start, since you can talk to your agent inside Archie itself. A chat app is what lets it reach you anywhere: your agent lives there like a contact, same conversation from your desk or your phone. Telegram is the quickest.

On a Mac, iMessage needs no account at all, and your agent answers in the conversation you have with yourself. WhatsApp is the one still missing, because it does not let an app like this answer on your behalf: its rule, not our choice. Either way, what your agent tells you crosses that company’s servers, so we are building Archie Mobile.

Setup

Your path to a running agent.

5 steps from a quiet computer to an agent you can message from anywhere, and one promise for whatever comes after.

  1. 01

    Pick a computer it can live on

    The one you already own probably qualifies. The whole list is above.

  2. 02

    Install Archie

    Download the desktop app and open it. Archie is in testing; the waitlist hears the day it opens. See where it stands →

  3. 03

    Meet your agent

    Name it and answer a few questions. It fits itself out from your answers, tells you what it added, and you can take any of it back off. Browse the marketplace when you want more.

  4. 04

    Connect your chat app

    Your agent gets its own account on Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix or, on a Mac, iMessage, and you message it the way you would message a person.

  5. 05

    Message it from anywhere

    It does the work on your computer and replies in your chat. It sends email and updates your calendar only after you approve each one, and it can’t spend money: that ability doesn’t exist in Archie at all.

  6. 06

    Hit a ceiling? Tell us

    If Archie can’t do it yet, we build the add-on, and every commissioned add-on becomes a marketplace listing.

2 ways in

On your own, or with us beside you.

You can do all of this yourself. Guided setup is for everyone who’d rather not do it alone.

Do it yourself

  • Install Archie and build your agent at your own pace
  • Every add-on is included with Archie
  • Connect only the accounts you choose; your keys live in your computer’s own password store (Keychain on a Mac, Credential Manager on Windows), where we have no way to read them
  • Hit a ceiling? Tell us, and we’ll build the add-on

Take the guided path

  • A free discovery call to map out what you want
  • We build with you over screen share, teaching every step in plain language
  • Bigger setups can take more than one session, and we tell you how many on that free call
  • Archie is $30 a month or $299 a year, separate from your sessions
  • Read more about guided setup
